dialogue.speaker: أحمد
dialogue.transliteration: kayfak alyoom ya 3amru?
dialogue.english: How are you today, Amr?

dialogue.speaker: عمرو
dialogue.transliteration: bi-khayr, il-7amdella. w inta?
dialogue.english: Well, thank God. And you?

dialogue.speaker: أحمد
dialogue.transliteration: ana shwayya ta3baan alyoom
dialogue.english: I'm a little tired today.

dialogue.speaker: عمرو
dialogue.transliteration: shnoo fika? feeh 7aaj madhaayigak?
dialogue.english: What's wrong? Is something bothering you?

dialogue.speaker: أحمد
dialogue.transliteration: aywah, 2ali2 3ala limti7aan bakkra
dialogue.english: Yes, I'm worried about tomorrow's exam.

dialogue.speaker: عمرو
dialogue.transliteration: la takhaf, inta daaris zayn
dialogue.english: Don't be scared, you've studied well.

dialogue.speaker: أحمد
dialogue.arabic: إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ، بَسْ أَنَا خَايِفْ شْوَيَّة
dialogue.transliteration: in shaa Allah, bas ana khayif shwayya
dialogue.english: God willing, but I'm a bit scared.

dialogue.speaker: عمرو
dialogue.arabic: أَنَا مَرْيُوحْ إِنَّك جِيتَ الْيَوْمَ. خَلِّنَا نِشْرَبْ شَايْ
dialogue.transliteration: ana maryoo7 innak jeeta alyoom. khallna nishrab shay
dialogue.english: I'm glad you came today. Let's have tea.

dialogue.speaker: أحمد
dialogue.arabic: تَمَام، وَأَنَا جَايِعْ وَايْد، أَبِي آكُل حَاجْ
dialogue.transliteration: tamaam, w ana jaa3i wayid, abi aakol 7aaj
dialogue.english: Good, and I'm very hungry, I want to eat something.

dialogue.speaker: عمرو
dialogue.arabic: يَلَّا نِرُوحْ الْمَطْعَمْ اللِّي بِقِرْبْ الْبَيْتْ
dialogue.transliteration: yalla niroo7 il-mat3am illi bi-girb il-bayt
dialogue.english: Come on, let's go to the restaurant near the house.

dialogue.speaker: أحمد
dialogue.arabic: يَلَّا، شُكْرًا. أَنَا مَرْيُوحْ إِنِّي شُفْتَكْ
dialogue.transliteration: yalla, shukran. ana maryoo7 inni shuftak
dialogue.english: Come on, thanks. I'm glad I saw you.

lessons.culture: In Yemen when asked "كيفك؟" people answer with "الحمد لله" or "بخير" out of habit, whatever they feel, and a close friend or family member will push further with "شنو فيك؟" if they seem worried. Saying you're "حزين" or "تعبان" plainly is normal only with people close to you.

exercises.prompt: Someone says: "كَيْفَكَ الْيَوْمَ؟". Give a natural reply.

too_formal.feedback: Correct but bookish; "الحمد لله" is the natural spoken answer.

exercises.tip: "الحمد لله" is added almost automatically after saying you're well.

exercises.prompt: Someone says: "شْنُو فِيكَ؟". Give a natural reply.
accepted: ما فيني حاج، بس تعبان شويه

too_formal.feedback: That is formal written Arabic, not how it's said in conversation.

exercises.tip: "شويه" softens the admission, like saying "a little".

exercises.prompt: Complete: "أَنَا ___ وَايْدْ، أَبِي آكُل حَاجْ." Meaning: I'm very hungry, I want to eat something.

too_formal.feedback: Formal way of stating hunger; "جايع" is the word actually used.

exercises.tip: "جايع/جايعة" changes with the speaker's gender.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "أَنَا ___ مِنْ هَالْحَاجْ." Meaning: I'm scared of this.

too_formal.feedback: Formal spelling and register; "خايف" is how it's said out loud.

exercises.tip: "خايف" for a man, "خايفة" for a woman.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I'm very happy today."

too_formal.feedback: "سعيد" is the formal word for happy; Yemenis say "مريوح".

exercises.tip: "مريوح" is the everyday word for happy, not "سعيد".

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I'm a little worried about the exam."

too_formal.item: أَنَا مُقْلِقٌ بَعْضَ الشَّيْءِ بِخُصُوصِ الِامْتِحَانِ
too_formal.feedback: Overly formal phrasing for a simple everyday worry.

exercises.tip: "شويه" is the fast way of softening the worry.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "I'm worried"?

too_formal.feedback: Nobody speaks like this out loud; it belongs in writing, not conversation.

exercises.tip: "قلق" comes from the same root as "قلق", worry.

exercises.prompt: "حَزِينْ" means:

too_formal.feedback: That is a dictionary-style gloss, not the plain answer expected here.

exercises.tip: "حزين" means sad; it's used when someone is genuinely sad.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "وَايْدْ / الْيَوْمَ / مَرْيُوحْ / أَنَا".

too_formal.feedback: Formal register and word order, not the conversational sentence being practiced.

exercises.tip: The subject "أنا" comes first, then the feeling, then how much, then when.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "مِنْ / خَايِفْ / هَالْحَاجْ / أَنَا".

too_formal.feedback: Formal spelling "خائف" and "هذا الأمر" instead of the spoken forms.

exercises.tip: "هالحاج" is the everyday contraction of "هذا الحاج".

dialogue.speaker: سلمى
dialogue.transliteration: bira2yi niroo7 il-madeena il-2adeema
dialogue.english: In my opinion, let's go to the old city.

dialogue.speaker: محمود
dialogue.transliteration: yimkin, bas il-jaw 7arr wayid
dialogue.english: Maybe, but the weather is very hot.

dialogue.speaker: سلمى
dialogue.arabic: أَنْتَ صَحِيحْ. شْنُو رَأْيَكْ فِي السّاحَةْ؟
dialogue.transliteration: anta sa7ee7. shnoo ra2yak fi is-saa7a?
dialogue.english: You're right. What's your opinion of the square?

dialogue.speaker: محمود
dialogue.arabic: لَا، مُو هِيكَ. السّاحَةْ مِلْيَانَة نَاسْ يَوْمْ الْجُمْعَةْ
dialogue.transliteration: la, mu heeka. is-saa7a milyaana nas yoom il-jum3a
dialogue.english: No, not like that, the square is full of people on Friday.

dialogue.speaker: سلمى
dialogue.arabic: صَحِيحْ، هَاد صَحِيحْ. خَلِّنَا نِرُوحْ بَعْدْ الْعَصِرْ
dialogue.transliteration: sa7ee7, haad sa7ee7. khallna niroo7 ba3d il-3asr
dialogue.english: True, that's right. Let's go after the afternoon prayer.

dialogue.speaker: محمود
dialogue.arabic: أَنَا مُوَافِقْ، بَعْدْ الْعَصِرْ الْجَوّْ أَحْسَنْ
dialogue.transliteration: ana muwaafi2, ba3d il-3asr il-jaw a7san
dialogue.english: I agree, after the afternoon the weather's better.

dialogue.speaker: سلمى
dialogue.transliteration: bid-dabt. wayn niroo7 bid-dabt?
dialogue.english: Exactly. Where exactly shall we go?

dialogue.speaker: محمود
dialogue.arabic: أَنَا مَا بُوَافِقَكْ عَلَى السّاحَةْ، الْبَازَارْ أَحْسَنْ
dialogue.transliteration: ana ma buwafi2ak 3ala is-saa7a, il-bazaar a7san
dialogue.english: I don't agree with you about the square, the bazaar is better.

dialogue.speaker: سلمى
dialogue.transliteration: tamaam, tamm, il-bazaar ahda w a7la
dialogue.english: OK, that works, the bazaar is quieter and nicer.

dialogue.speaker: محمود
dialogue.transliteration: bas laazim nijib shay ma3aana
dialogue.english: But we must bring tea with us.

dialogue.speaker: سلمى
dialogue.arabic: أَنْتَ صَحِيحْ، أَنَا بِجِيبْ الْمَاءْ الْبَارِدْ
dialogue.transliteration: anta sa7ee7, ana bijiib il-maa il-baarid
dialogue.english: You're right, I'll bring the cold water.

response.english: In my opinion we go now.

pair.english: Do you agree with the plan?

lessons.culture: In Yemen a flat "لا" can sound blunt, so people soften a disagreement with "يمكن، بس" or "تمام، بس" before giving their view. "تمام" and "تمّ" are the light way to say OK, and "أنت صحيح" is warm enough to use with elders and friends alike.

exercises.prompt: Someone says: "شْنُو رَأْيَكْ؟". Give a natural reply.

too_formal.feedback: Grammatically fine but too formal for a casual answer.

exercises.tip: "برأيي" attaches "my opinion" directly to the front of the sentence.

exercises.prompt: Someone says: "أَنْتَ مُوَافِقْ؟". Give a natural reply saying no.

too_formal.feedback: Formal negation "كلا"; "لا" is the spoken word for no.

exercises.tip: "مو موافق" is another way to say it.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "___ صَحِيحْ، هِيكَ أَحْسَنْ." Meaning: You're right, this is better.

too_formal.feedback: "على حق" is the formal form; "أنت صحيح" is the spoken phrase.

exercises.tip: "أنت صحيح" is the everyday way to say someone's right.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "أَنَا ___، خَلِّينِي أَفِكِّرْ شْوَيَّةْ." Meaning: Maybe, let me think a little.

too_formal.feedback: Formal phrasing; "يمكن" alone is how this is actually said.

exercises.tip: "يمكن" is used constantly to soften an answer that isn't a clear yes.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I don't agree with you."

too_formal.feedback: That's the formal written way of disagreeing.

exercises.tip: "ما بوافقك" needs no extra pronoun; the verb already carries "I".

exercises.prompt: Translate: "OK, that works."

too_formal.feedback: Overly formal for accepting a plan in conversation.

exercises.tip: "تمام" or "تمّ" are the light ways to agree in Yemen.

exercises.prompt: Which phrase means "I agree" said by a woman?

too_formal.feedback: Formal, and does not mark gender the way spoken Yemeni does.

exercises.tip: "موافقة" ends in ة for a woman speaking; "موافق" is for a man.

exercises.prompt: "هَاد مُو صَحِيحْ" means:

too_formal.feedback: That's a formal restatement, not the plain meaning asked for.

exercises.tip: "مو" is the everyday negation used before nouns and adjectives.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "صَحِيحْ / أَنْتَ".

too_formal.feedback: "على حق" is formal Arabic; "أنت صحيح" is what's actually said.

exercises.tip: "أنت" comes first, then "صحيح".

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "الْقَدِيمَةْ / الْمَدِينَةْ / نِرُوحْ / بِرَأْيِي".

too_formal.item: فِي رَأْيِي، سَنَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْمَدِينَةِ الْقَدِيمَةِ
too_formal.feedback: Formal wording and word order not used in daily speech.

exercises.tip: "برأيي" opens the sentence; then the plan.

phrases.arabic: لَوْ كُنْتَ مَكَانِي كُنْتَ سَوِّيتْ هِيكَ
phrases.transliteration: law kunta makani kunta sawweet heeka

dialogue.speaker: منى
dialogue.arabic: شْنُو فِيكَ يَا فَهَدْ؟ شَكْلَكَ تَعْبَان
dialogue.transliteration: shnoo fika ya fahad? shaklak ta3baan
dialogue.english: What's wrong, Fahad? You look tired.

dialogue.speaker: فهد
dialogue.transliteration: aywah, 3indi suda3 min yoomeen
dialogue.english: Yes, I've had a headache for two days.

dialogue.speaker: منى
dialogue.transliteration: lazim tiroo7 lid-duktoor, ma tita2akhkhar
dialogue.english: You should go to the doctor, don't delay.

dialogue.speaker: فهد
dialogue.transliteration: ma abi, akeed 7aaj basi6a
dialogue.english: I don't want to, it's surely something simple.

dialogue.speaker: منى
dialogue.arabic: لِيشْ مَا تِجَرِّبْ هَالدَّوَاءْ؟ عِنْدِي وَاحِدْ مَنْيِحْ
dialogue.transliteration: leesh ma tijarrib hal-dawaa? 3indi waa7id manee7
dialogue.english: Why don't you try this medicine? I have a good one.

dialogue.speaker: فهد
dialogue.arabic: مَا يِضِرّْ، بَسْ أَنَا مَا أَحِبّْ الدَّوَاءْ
dialogue.transliteration: ma yidiRR, bas ana ma a7ibb id-dawaa
dialogue.english: No harm, but I don't like medicine.

dialogue.speaker: منى
dialogue.arabic: اِسْمَعْ نَصِيحْتِي، خُدْ بَالَكْ مِنْ نَفْسَكْ
dialogue.transliteration: isma3 nasee7ti, khod balak min nafsak
dialogue.english: Listen to my advice, take care of yourself.

dialogue.speaker: فهد
dialogue.arabic: تَمَام، بَسْ مَا فِيهْ وَقِتْ، عِنْدِي شُغِلْ وَايْدْ
dialogue.transliteration: tamaam, bas ma feeh wa2it, 3indi shughil wayid
dialogue.english: OK, but there's no time, I have a lot of work.

dialogue.speaker: منى
dialogue.arabic: لَوْ كُنْتَ مَكَانِي كُنْتَ رُحْتَ الْآنْ
dialogue.transliteration: law kunta makani kunta ru7t il-aan
dialogue.english: If I were you, I'd have gone now.

dialogue.speaker: فهد
dialogue.arabic: أَنْتِ صَحِيحَةْ، بِرُوحْ بَعْدْ الشُّغِلْ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ
dialogue.transliteration: anti sa7ee7a, biroo7 ba3d ish-shughil in shaa Allah
dialogue.english: You're right, I'll go after work, God willing.

dialogue.speaker: منى
dialogue.transliteration: tamaam, khallik haadi, alla yishafi2ak
dialogue.english: Good, stay calm, may God heal you.

lessons.culture: Yemeni friends and relatives give advice openly and warmly with "لازم" and "خد بالك", and it is taken as care, not criticism. After someone mentions being ill, the usual reply is "الله يشافيك", may God heal you.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "Take care of yourself" (to a man)?

too_formal.feedback: Formal; "خد بالك" is the spoken "take care".

exercises.tip: "خد بالك" literally turns your attention; it also means watch out.

exercises.prompt: How is a woman told "You should rest"?

too_formal.feedback: Formal; "لازم" is the spoken "should".

exercises.tip: The feminine ending in Yemen is "ي": ترتاح (m), ترتاحي (f).

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "لِلدُّكْتُورْ / تِرُوحْ / لَازِمْ".

too_formal.feedback: Formal; speakers say "دكتور" and "تروح".

exercises.tip: "لازم" goes first, then the verb.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "هَالدَّوَاءْ / تِجَرِّبْ / مَا / لِيشْ".

too_formal.feedback: Formal; speakers say "ليش ما".

exercises.tip: "ليش ما" plus a verb is the friendly way to suggest something.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "___ بَالَكْ مِنْ نَفْسَكْ." Meaning: Take care of yourself.

too_formal.feedback: Formal; "خد بالك" is what is said.

exercises.tip: To a woman: "خدي بالج من نفسج".

exercises.prompt: Complete: "مَا ___ تِجَرِّبْ." Meaning: It won't hurt you to try.

too_formal.feedback: A formal, written way to say it.

exercises.tip: "يضرك" is "hurts you"; "ما يضرك" means no harm done.

exercises.prompt: Someone says: "عِنْدِي صُدَاعْ مِنْ يَوْمَيْنْ". Give a natural piece of advice.

too_formal.feedback: Bookish; "لازم تروح للدكتور" is the spoken advice.

exercises.tip: Advice starts with "لازم" or "الأحسن".

exercises.prompt: Someone says: "أَنَا تَعْبَان وَايْدْ". Give a natural piece of advice.

too_formal.item: يَنْبَغِي لَكَ أَنْ تَأْخُذَ قِسْطًا مِنَ الرَّاحَةِ
too_formal.feedback: Very formal; "لازم ترتاح" is what friends say.

exercises.tip: "شويه" softens the advice.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "Try this medicine."

too_formal.feedback: "عقار" is a written word; speakers say "دواء".

exercises.tip: "هالدواء" is short for "هذا الدواء".

exercises.prompt: Translate: "Stay calm and don't rush."

too_formal.feedback: Formal; "خليك هادي" is the spoken word.

exercises.tip: "وما" joins two commands: calm down, and do not rush.

phrases.arabic: الْأَكِل بَارِدْ شْوَيَّةْ، تِقْدَرْ تِسْخِّنِهْ لِي؟
phrases.transliteration: il-akil baarid shwayya, tigdar tisakhkhinha li?

phrases.arabic: مَا قَصْدِي أُزْعِجَكْ، بَسْ هَاد مُهِمّْ
هَاد مَا هُوّْ مِثِلْ اللِّي شُفْتِهْ بِالصّورَةْ
phrases.transliteration: haad ma hoo mithl illi shuftih bis-suura

phrases.arabic: مَا فِي مِشْكِلَةْ، بَسْ أَبِي أُوَضِّحْ
phrases.transliteration: ma fi mishkila, bas abi awaDDe7

dialogue.speaker: يوسف
dialogue.transliteration: law sama7t, fi mishkila sghira
dialogue.english: Excuse me, I have a small problem.

dialogue.speaker: علي
dialogue.transliteration: tafaDDal, shnoo il-mishkila?
dialogue.english: Go ahead, what's the problem?

dialogue.speaker: يوسف
dialogue.arabic: آسِفْ عَلَى الْإِزْعَاجْ، بَسْ هَاد مَا هُوّْ اللِّي طَلَبْتِهْ
dialogue.transliteration: asif 3ala l-iz3aaj, bas haad ma hoo illi talabtiih
dialogue.english: Sorry to bother you, but this isn't what I ordered.

dialogue.speaker: علي
dialogue.transliteration: asif wayid, shnoo talabta?
dialogue.english: Very sorry, what did you order?

dialogue.speaker: يوسف
dialogue.transliteration: talabtu dijaj mashwi, w haad la7im
dialogue.english: I ordered grilled chicken, and this is meat.

dialogue.speaker: علي
dialogue.transliteration: la7da, aghayyyirah lak il-aan
dialogue.english: One moment, I'll change it for you now.

dialogue.speaker: يوسف
dialogue.arabic: وَكِمَان الْأَكِل بَارِدْ شْوَيَّةْ، تِقْدَرْ تِسْخِّنِهْ لِي؟
dialogue.transliteration: w kiman il-akil baarid shwayya, tigdar tisakhkhinha li?
dialogue.english: Also the food is a bit cold, can you heat it up for me?

dialogue.speaker: علي
dialogue.transliteration: akeed, w asif it-talab ta2akhkhar
dialogue.english: Of course, and sorry the order was late.

dialogue.speaker: يوسف
dialogue.arabic: مَا عَلَيْكَ، بَسْ فِي غَلِطَةْ بِالْحِسَابْ كِمَان
dialogue.transliteration: ma 3aleek, bas fi ghali6a bil-7isab kiman
dialogue.english: No worries, but there's a mistake in the bill too.

dialogue.speaker: علي
dialogue.arabic: خَلِّينِي أَشُوفْ الْحِسَابْ. صَحِيحْ، أَنْتَ صَحِيحْ، بِصَلِّحُهْ لَكْ
dialogue.transliteration: khalliini ashuuf il-7isab. sa7ee7, anta sa7ee7, bisalli7ah lak
dialogue.english: Let me see the bill. True, you're right, I'll fix it for you.

dialogue.speaker: يوسف
dialogue.transliteration: shukran, alla yi36i2ak il-3aafya
dialogue.english: Thank you, may God give you strength.

pair.english: Excuse me, can you help me?

response.english: Go ahead, what do you want?
Sorry, I'll change it for you now.

pair.english: There's a mistake in the bill.

response.english: A thousand sorries, I'll fix it.

lessons.culture: A complaint in Yemen starts calmly with "لو سمحت" or "آسف على الإزعاج", and raising your voice is seen as rude. Staff answer with "آسف" and fix it, and it is common to thank them with "الله يعطيك العافية".

exercises.prompt: Which sentence opens a polite complaint (to a man)?

too_formal.feedback: Correct but formal; "لو سمحت، في" is what is said.

exercises.tip: Always start with "لو سمحت" before the problem.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "There's a mistake in the bill"?

too_formal.feedback: Formal; "في غلطة بالحساب" is the spoken form.

exercises.tip: "في" means there is; "الحساب" is the bill.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "طَلَبْتِهْ / اللِّي / هُوّْ / مَا / هَاد".

too_formal.feedback: Formal; speakers say "مو اللي".

exercises.tip: "اللي" means what or which; "ما هو" is the spoken not.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "هَالْمَوْضُوعْ / فِي / تِسَاعِدْنِي / تِقْدَرْ".

too_formal.item: هَلْ يُمْكِنُكَ مُسَاعَدَتِي فِي هَذَا الْأَمْرِ
too_formal.feedback: Formal; speakers say "تقدر" for can you.

exercises.tip: "تقدر" is how "can you" is asked in Yemen.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "الْأَكِل بَارِدْ شْوَيَّةْ، تِقْدَرْ ___ لِي؟" Meaning: The food is a bit cold, can you heat it up for me?

too_formal.feedback: Formal; "تسخنه لي" is spoken.

exercises.tip: "سخّن" means to heat; "تسخنه" is you heat it.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "الطَّلَبْ ___ وَايْدْ." Meaning: The order is very late.

too_formal.feedback: Formal; "متأخر وايد" is how it is said.

exercises.tip: "وايد" after an adjective means very.

exercises.prompt: A waiter says: "تَفَضَّلْ، شْنُو الْمِشْكِلَةْ؟". Give a natural reply.

too_formal.feedback: Formal; the spoken form is short and direct.

exercises.tip: Say the problem in one short sentence, with no blame.

exercises.prompt: Someone says: "الْأَكِل بَارِدْ شْوَيَّةْ". Reply as the waiter.

too_formal.feedback: Formal; "آسف" and "الآن" are what is said.

exercises.tip: "الآن" means now in Yemen.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "Can you refund my money?"

too_formal.feedback: Formal; "فلوسي" is my money in speech.

exercises.tip: "ترد" means to give back.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "Sorry to bother you, but..." (m)

too_formal.feedback: Formal; "بس" replaces "ولكن" in speech.

exercises.tip: Apologise first, then "بس" and the request.

challenge.title: A Day Out
challenge.instructions: Write a short conversation between two friends who meet. One asks how the other feels, hears about a worry, gives advice, they agree on a plan, and then one politely raises a small complaint at a restaurant.
required_elements: a question asking how someone feels, using "كيفك" or "كيفك"
at least one feeling word such as "تعبان", "مريوح" or "قلق"
a piece of advice using "لازم" or "الأحسن"
agreement or disagreement using "أنت صحيح" or "ما موافق"
a polite complaint opened with "لو سمحت" or "آسف على الإزعاج"

dialogue.speaker: هالة
dialogue.transliteration: kayfak alyoom?
dialogue.english: How are you today?

dialogue.speaker: عمر
dialogue.arabic: أَنَا شْوَيَّة قَلِقْ، عِنْدِي شُغِلْ وَايْدْ
dialogue.transliteration: ana shwayya 2ali2, 3indi shughil wayid
dialogue.english: I'm a little worried, I have a lot of work.

dialogue.speaker: هالة
dialogue.arabic: الْأَحْسَنْ تِرْتَاحْ شْوَيَّةْ قَبْلْ مَا تِتَعَبّْ أَكْتَرْ
dialogue.transliteration: il-a7san tirtaa7 shwayya 2abl ma tita3ab aktar
dialogue.english: It's better you rest a little before you get more tired.

dialogue.speaker: عمر
dialogue.transliteration: anti sa7ee7a, khallna niroo7 nitaghadd
dialogue.english: You're right, let's go have lunch.

dialogue.speaker: هالة
dialogue.transliteration: tamaam, tamm, w ana jaa3a wayid
dialogue.english: OK, that works, and I'm very hungry.

dialogue.speaker: عمر
dialogue.arabic: لَوْ سَمَحْتَ، هَاد مَا هُوّْ اللِّي طَلَبْتِهْ
dialogue.transliteration: law sama7t, haad ma hoo illi talabtiih
dialogue.english: Excuse me, this isn't what I ordered.

dialogue.speaker: الخادم
dialogue.transliteration: asif wayid, aghayyyirah lak il-aan
dialogue.english: Very sorry, I'll change it for you now.

dialogue.speaker: عمر
dialogue.transliteration: shukran, alla yi36i2ak il-3aafya
dialogue.english: Thank you, may God give you strength.
